transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because for the past year or so, I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. 

I'm a phlebotomist, so I know what I'm looking at. No matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I actually saw. Nobody will listen to me, and honestly, trying to get people to see the truth is just... it's wearing me down.
Aside from your concerns about the lab results, have you noticed anything unusual with your senses—like hearing voices, seeing things, or sensing things that others don't seem to notice?

No, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My senses are completely normal. The only thing I'm seeing is the actual data in the system that someone is messing with. But no, no voices or anything like that.
Does anyone else in your life—like a family member or close friend—share this same belief that your dad's lab results are being altered, or is this something only you have noticed?

No, it's really just me. My family... they don't get it. I mean, they don't work in a lab, so they just look at the final printout and trust whatever the doctor tells them. 

I'm the only one who actually knows how to read the raw data and understands how the reporting system works. So, yeah, no one else sees it. They just think I can't let it go.

Outside of this situation with your dad's lab results, how has your day-to-day life been going—are you still functioning well at work and in your relationships, or has this been affecting other areas of your life too?

Everything else is fine, honestly. Outside of the dispute about my dad's records, my life is pretty normal. I still go to all my phlebotomy shifts, pay my bills, take care of myself... I manage all my normal day-to-day responsibilities without any issues. 

It takes up a lot of my mental energy because it's so frustrating, but it hasn't stopped me from doing what I need to do or living my life. Work is fine, everything else is fine. It's really just this one specific thing.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a fixed, non-bizarre delusional belief (that a lab technician is altering her father's medical records) that has persisted for approximately one year. There are no hallucinations, no other perceptual disturbances, and no evidence of disorganized speech or behavior. The delusion is circumscribed to this single theme, is not shared by others (ruling out shared delusion), and overall functioning—work, self-care, relationships—remains intact aside from distress and preoccupation related to the delusion. This presentation is consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22), persecutory/mixed type, rather than schizophrenia (which requires broader psychotic symptoms and functional decline) or a mood disorder with psychotic features (no mood symptoms reported). Paranoid personality disorder was considered but ruled out given the presence of a fixed, encapsulated delusional belief rather than a pervasive, longstanding pattern of distrust across multiple contexts.
